scenes.say: Elon Musk's car company and his rocket company could become one.
A giant worth about 3.5 trillion dollars.
scenes.speak: A giant worth about three and a half trillion dollars.

scenes.say: Tesla and SpaceX: why Musk wants to merge them.
scenes.title: One company?

scenes.say: Asked if a merger made sense, Musk said one word.
Yes.
Special committees have now been set up to study a deal.
But Musk says there's no certainty, and no agreement yet.
Tesla is valued at about 1.5 trillion dollars. SpaceX, around 2 trillion.
scenes.speak: Tesla is valued at about one and a half trillion dollars. SpaceX, around two trillion.

scenes.say: Together, nearly 3.5 trillion: one of the biggest mergers ever.
scenes.speak: Together, nearly three and a half trillion: one of the biggest mergers ever.
scenes.label: Combined value, approx.

scenes.say: So why do it?
Musk says there's a lot to be gained from working together.
scenes.text: There's a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass-to-orbit… connectivity.

scenes.say: Take Terafab, his chip project: chips for Tesla's cars and robots, and SpaceX's data centres.
scenes.title: One chip plant, two companies

scenes.say: He hopes it starts volume production by late 2028.
scenes.speak: He hopes it starts volume production by late twenty twenty-eight.

scenes.say: Tesla's batteries could power SpaceX's hungry computers.
And Starlink could connect Tesla's robotaxis and robots.
Tesla's factory know-how could help SpaceX build Starship at scale.
scenes.title: Building Starship

scenes.say: For investors, one share would buy into everything.
Cars, batteries, robots, rockets and satellite internet.
scenes.title: What you'd own

scenes.say: But also, every risk at once.
SpaceX works for the US military, intelligence agencies and NASA.
Tesla has a big business in China, including its Shanghai factory.
Together, they could draw scrutiny in Washington, and strain ties with Beijing.
Then shareholders must agree, and the big projects are costly and unproven.
scenes.title: The hurdles

scenes.say: A merger wouldn't make those risks go away.
scenes.title: The risks stay

scenes.say: For now, it's an idea Musk likes, not a deal.
